title: Required Reading
summary: This week: Nancy Spero’s pro-choice art, Valentina Di Liscia on “Casa Cueva,” Brooklyn’s smallest museum, Jamaica Kincaid’s eyebrows, Israeli cuisine and Palestinian erasure, and more.

title: 24 Latin American Art Scholars Named ISLAA Fellows
summary: New leaders at the Portland Art Museum and Storm King Art Center, a West Coast art magazine closes, and more in this week's Art Movements.

title: Former Philly UArts Building to Become Affordable Housing for Artists
summary: The Village of Industry & Art will transform a dormitory in the now-shuttered university into 45 affordable units by fall 2027.

title: Six Films on Art and Resistance at BlackStar Film Festival
summary: The Philadelphia festival platformed films on Anishinaabe repatriation, the spirited life of art historian Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the Puerto Rican history of the Upper West Side, and more.

title: A Picasso Vanished in 1961. The Guggenheim Now Wants It Back
summary: The museum is suing the current owners of "Femme dans un fauteuil" (1918), which resurfaced decades after it was stolen from the University of Pittsburgh.

title: Long-Misattributed Clara Peeters Still Life Resurfaces After Decades in Storage
summary: Formerly attributed to the Brueghel family, the painting was found in 2022 by a curator at the National Museum of Norway.

title: A New Chapter for Zeitz MOCAA
summary: Elvira Dyangani Ose is named artistic director of the Cape Town museum, following in the late Koyo Kouoh’s footsteps.

title: SF Camerawork, Photo Champion for Five Decades, Abruptly Announces Closure
summary: The nonprofit's co-founder, photographer Hal Fischer, told Hyperallergic that neither he nor anyone he knew “got advance warning that this was in the wind.”

title: “American Doctor” Is an Indictment of US Leadership and Media
summary: The new documentary follows three humanitarian physicians as they grapple with the horrors of the US-funded genocide in Gaza.

title: The Living World Feels Dead at the Hammer
summary: “Several Eternities” feels overly careful and unable to combust as fully as it could have.

title: Elvira Dyangani Ose to Succeed Koyo Kouoh at Zeitz MOCAA
summary: The Spanish curator will steer the South African institution after the untimely loss of its late leader.

title: Remembering Christian Bernard, Al Gury, and Hermione Carline
summary: This week, we honor the founding museum director, an artist who shaped PAFA, and a painter of transience.

title: Meet This Year’s Joan Mitchell Fellows
summary: 15 artists won this year’s prize. Plus, an interview with the founder of BlackStar Film Festival, layoffs at the San Diego Museum of Art, and more.

title: 15 Artists Named 2026 Joan Mitchell Fellows
summary: Each recipient will receive $60,000 in unrestricted funding distributed over five years, in the spirit of the namesake abstract painter’s commitment to “aid and assist” artists.

title: Art Dispatches From “Habibi City”
summary: Alan Michelson’s oyster-shaped public artwork on Governors Island, a fragment of The Odyssey at The Met, and Simone Forti talking about her days in Yoko Ono’s Manhattan loft.
